newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open stronger, keep firm tone.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open stronger, keep firm tone.

text.p: An upbeat Australian share market opened stronger on Monday, extending Friday's impressive gains after Wall Street continued to rally although early volumes were light.
The All Ordinaries index added 5.2 points to 2,447.6.

Residual buying interest from Friday's hectic trade, and investors heartened by Wall Street's firmer finish, gave the initial impetus as the market awaited local March quarter inflation figures, due Wednesday.

"I think some left over interest and probably some fresh interest on the back of Wall Street," said Andrew Sekely, head of equities at brokerage Intersuisse, although he noted the persistent discount of futures to the underlying market.
"Unfortunately, the futures are still selling at a discount which is a bit surprising, but by and large the market is in reasonably good shape."
With the leaders posting nondescript gains, the attention was on the smaller end with impressive drilling results putting a shine on several explorers.
Carpenter Pacific Resources NL and Ramsgate Resources NL jumped straight out of the blocks as traders digested promising drilling results from the Mt Kare project in Papua New Guinea.

Carpenter shares were 21 percent higher at 46 cents (US36 cents) with over seven million shares traded early while Ramsgate shares were 16 percent higher at 11 cents. Ramsgate trade was also active with over 10 million shares traded.
Fellow gold explorers Arcadia Minerals NL and Sipa Resources NL also climbed high after well-received drilling results from their Mt Olympus gold prospect in Western Australia.
Arcadia climbed 25 percent to 99 cents, albeit on thin trade, while Sipa also jumped 25 percent to 60 cents early before slippping from its highs to be up eight cents at 56.
Rises outnumberdd falls by a ratio of about nine to four, while 43 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
